summary: Environment A evidence for Production Integration (OBS/vMix) - a real obs-websocket v5 client and a real vMix HTTP API client, each pushing CIP's currently-displayed presentation text into an operator-configured text source/title, wired as a best-effort sink alongside the existing local display broadcast.
auditFinding: docs/phase-4-master-plan-gap-audit.md and docs/phase-7-audit.md both graded OBS/vMix/livestream integration NOT STARTED - integrations/obs and integrations/vmix were 6-line placeholder crates. See docs/phase-8-audit.md.
designChoice: Three real decisions, all resolved in the audit: (1) scope is text/title push only, never scene switching or recording/streaming control; (2) a fresh connection per push, not a persistent session, which also makes config live-editable without a restart; (3) best-effort on a dedicated worker thread, never fatal to CIP's own local display.
protocolChoice: obs-websocket v5 (real Hello/Identify/Identified handshake, SHA256 challenge/response auth, SetInputSettings request) over plain ws://; vMix's real HTTP SetText API over plain http://. Both local-network-only by design, so no TLS backend is needed or pulled in.

newCode.obsCrate: integrations/obs/src/lib.rs: ObsTarget/ObsError, push_text (real handshake + auth + SetInputSettings request/response).
newCode.vmixCrate: integrations/vmix/src/lib.rs: VmixTarget/VmixError, push_text (real SetText GET request).
newCode.productionRs: apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/production.rs: ProductionIntegrationConfig/ProductionIntegrationStatus (in AppState, both in-memory Mutex, default disabled), push_to_configured_targets (best-effort, worker-thread, no-op when nothing configured), slide_push_text, test_obs_connection/test_vmix_connection.
newCode.commandsRs: apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/commands.rs: set_production_integration_config, get_production_integration_status, test_obs_connection, test_vmix_connection - wired into display_presentation and clear_active_presentation, the same two call sites broadcast_to_live_screens already uses.
newCode.frontend: domain/production.ts; commands.ts wrappers; new components/workspace/ProductionIntegrationPanel.tsx, wired into LiveChurchBrain.tsx only.

obsCrateTests: push_text succeeds against a real handshake with no password
push_text succeeds against a real handshake with a correct password
push_text reports auth required when OBS wants a password and none is configured
push_text surfaces a real OBS request failure honestly
push_text reports a clear error when nothing is listening
compute_auth_response matches the documented obs-websocket v5 algorithm
vmixCrateTests: push_text succeeds against a real HTTP 200 and sends the right query string
push_text surfaces a non-2xx status honestly
push_text reports a clear error when nothing is listening
newTests.testingBoundaryNote: Both crates are proven against real, protocol-correct in-process servers (a real tungstenite WebSocket handshake for OBS; a hand-rolled HTTP/1.1 server for vMix), not mock traits. production.rs's own worker-thread dispatch is thin glue over these already-tested clients and follows this codebase's established no-redundant-command-level-tests discipline (see commands.rs's test-module header, and Phase 7.3's identical reasoning).
frontendNewTests: setProductionIntegrationConfig forwards the config object as-is
testObsConnection/testVmixConnection forward their target objects as-is
rejects setProductionIntegrationConfig/getProductionIntegrationStatus/testObsConnection/testVmixConnection outside the Tauri runtime, without calling invoke()
newTests.command: cargo test -p cip-integrations-obs -p cip-integrations-vmix && npm run test -- --run

dependencyAudit.verificationMethod: cargo tree -p cip-integrations-obs and cargo tree -p cip-integrations-vmix, grepped for tls/ring/rustls - no matches. ureq's default tls/gzip features were explicitly disabled in the workspace Cargo.toml after an initial build showed they pulled in rustls/ring/webpki-roots; re-verified clean after disabling.
dependencyAudit.rationale: OBS/vMix are local-network-only by design (never wss:// or https://), so no TLS backend is needed - matches this project's established preference for pure-Rust dependencies wherever the actual protocol allows it (the same reasoning Phase 7.1 used for rustfft/hound over any C-toolchain alternative).

fullRegression.fmt: cargo fmt --all -- --check: clean (after one cargo fmt --all pass)
fullRegression.clippy: cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings: clean, both feature configs (default and --features whisper)
fullRegression.check: cargo check --workspace: clean, both feature configs
fullRegression.test: cargo test --workspace: all crates passing, both feature configs, zero regressions
fullRegression.frontend: npm run typecheck/lint/test/build: all clean - same 5 pre-existing lint warnings as before this phase, no new ones

architecturalSafetyNotes: Exactly four new Tauri commands, zero new events, zero new database schema.
core/presentation and core/music (domain contract crates) are untouched - this phase adds a new sink, not a new domain concept.

broadcast_to_live_screens and every existing DisplayScreen/RouteMode code path are byte-identical to before this phase - the production push is purely additive alongside the existing broadcast, never a replacement.
production_integration_config/production_integration_status are in-memory only, defaulting to disabled - a build with nothing configured behaves identically to before this phase.

File/config-write ordering: a push failure is caught, logged, and recorded in status - never propagated as an error from display_presentation/clear_presentation_display, and never blocks or delays those commands' own return.
honestLimitation: Text/title push only - no scene switching, no source visibility toggling, no recording/streaming control, no NDI output. Config does not persist across restarts. vMix's own SetText API returns a bare HTTP 200 regardless of whether the named input/field actually exists - a property of vMix's own API, not a gap in this client. Neither OBS nor vMix is installed in this container, so neither client has ever been exercised against the real applications.
